decisions.reason: Under-bowl service access does not necessarily change the accepted enclosure size, thickness, or overall form.
The client explicitly extends structural stability to the upper tower's rigidity and vibration during operation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Nolan, it’s exciting to see the machine progressing from separate parts into an integrated system. The overall form is coming together well, and the curved spout and tower design looks cleaner and more product-oriented than I imagined from the earlier renders. I also like being able to see the drainage routing and plumbing integrated beneath the bowl; functional details are now being resolved physically instead of only in CAD.

As work continues, I’m still considering splash control when the whisk runs at higher RPMs, the upper tower’s rigidity and vibration during operation, cleaning and sanitation access for every liquid-contact component, and access beneath the bowl for future servicing or maintenance.

Overall, this feels increasingly like a real product rather than merely a concept. I’m looking forward to the upcoming videos and testing footage.

Elena Marlowe

value_updates.upper_tower_stability: The upper tower must provide rigidity and control vibration during operation.

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY requiring cleaning and sanitation access for every liquid-contact component.
The source praises the integrated drainage routing but does not change the required pour behavior, flow quality, dispensing path, or beverage preservation.
Access beneath the bowl for servicing does not entail a change to the separate raised base, cup clearance, height, or footprint requirements.
The maintenance-access decision does not change compatibility requirements for shafts, couplings, controllers, or the power system.
Under-bowl service access is distinct from removing or rapidly swapping the bowls, and the source does not modify bowl-removal behavior.
The source does not alter electrical load, power-supply headroom, simultaneous loads, or cooling requirements.
The existing state already requires splash control across the approved higher-speed motor range, so the source reiterates rather than changes this requirement.
The source mentions high-RPM whisk operation only in relation to splash control and does not change the selected whisk design, material, size, or powder suitability.
Visible plumbing and service access beneath the bowl do not change the requirement that the bowl seal prevent liquid from reaching electronics.
The source does not modify the leak-containment behavior of the plumbing or bowl seals.
